title: Improving compatibility in mixed-matrix membranes - Nature Energy
gist: Nature Energy News & Views (paywalled preview) by Mariolino Carta on mixed-matrix membranes for carbon capture: new research shows that tailoring polymer–covalent organic framework (COF) interfaces fixes polymer–filler incompatibility, enabling high filler loadings and better CO2-separation membranes. Only the standfirst is accessible; no performance figures are given.

insights.claim: Mixed-matrix membranes for gas separation aim to combine the processability of polymers with the transport advantages of porous fillers, but poor compatibility between polymer and filler has limited their performance.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Polymer–filler incompatibility is the known bottleneck; any credible fix moves membrane carbon capture closer to deployment.
insights.quote: poor compatibility between the two limits their performance

insights.claim: New research reported in Nature Energy shows that tailoring the interfaces between polymers and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) enables high filler loadings and produces improved membranes for carbon capture.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Watch COF-based membrane developers and membrane carbon-capture players; interface engineering is the claimed lever, but no performance data are in the preview.
insights.quote: tailoring interfaces between polymers and covalent organic frameworks enables high filler loadings
insights.locator: New research shows that tailoring interfaces

insights.claim: Tuning the strength of the polymer–COF interfacial interaction is presented as the control knob for mixed-matrix membrane performance.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Interfacial chemistry, not just filler choice, determines whether high-loading membranes work; a useful diligence question for membrane startups.
insights.quote: Tuning polymer–COF interfacial interaction strength controls membrane performance
